core_obligations: Define T' as the complement in V of the maximal open over which f|_U is an isomorphism, note T and T' are disjoint closed subsets, and find constructible closed T_c containing T and T'_c containing T' with T_c cap T'_c empty by choosing suitable quasi-compact opens (proof lines 9620-9629).

Blow up so that the closures of T_c and T'_c become disjoint, using the separation lemma, then set Y_0 as the complement of the closure of T'_c with V_0 = V setminus T'_c, U_0 = U x_V V_0 and X_0 = X x_Y Y_0 (proof lines 9630-9634).

Since U_0 -> V_0 is an isomorphism, apply the Zariski-after-blowup lemma to obtain a V_0-admissible blowing up Y'_0 -> Y_0 over which the strict transform X'_0 of X_0 maps isomorphically (proof lines 9635-9638).

Lift the local solution: by the extension result for admissible blowups there is a V-admissible blowup Y' -> Y restricting to Y'_0 -> Y_0, and the strict transform f' : X' -> Y' is an isomorphism over the neighbourhood Y'_0 of the closure of T (proof lines 9639-9643).
proof_roadmap: Isolate the obstruction and separate it from T by constructible sets (proof lines 9620-9629).
Blow up to disjoint closures and set up the local isomorphism situation over Y_0 (proof lines 9630-9638).
Lift the V_0-admissible blowing up to a V-admissible blowing up of Y (proof lines 9639-9643).
difficulty_reason: For a proper morphism f : X -> Y of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, a quasi-compact open V of Y with preimage U, and a closed subset T of V over a neighbourhood of which f|_U is an isomorphism, the lemma produces a V-admissible blowing up Y' -> Y such that the strict transform f' : X' -> Y' is an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of the closure of T in Y' (statement lines 9607-9617). The proof isolates the obstruction as the closed subset T' where f|_U fails to be an isomorphism, disjoint from T, and then separates the two by constructible approximations: since V is spectral one finds constructible closed T_c containing T and T'_c containing T' with empty intersection, explicitly via quasi-compact opens (proof lines 9620-9629). A disjoint-locally-closed separation lemma lets one blow up so that the two closures become disjoint, after which the complement Y_0 of the closure of T'_c carries a V_0-admissible blowing up making the strict transform an isomorphism by the Zariski-after-blowup lemma, and an extension result for admissible blowups lifts that local solution back to a V-admissible blowing up of Y (proof lines 9630-9643). Separating the obstruction from T by constructible approximations and then lifting the local solution is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
